nodes.label: User
nodes.summary: Opens the app and gets a ranked list; their watches, searches and impressions become the next training data.

nodes.label: Recommendation API
nodes.summary: Receives a request with user and context, calls the stages, returns the list, and logs impressions and actions. Industry practice.

nodes.label: Candidate generation
nodes.summary: Narrows millions of items to hundreds using a learned user embedding and nearest-neighbour search, and can blend other candidate sources.

nodes.label: User model
nodes.summary: Neural network that turns watch history, search history, demographics, geography, device and example age into a user embedding.

nodes.label: Nearest-neighbour search
nodes.summary: Approximate search in the dot-product space over video embeddings, sublinear in the number of items, within tens of milliseconds. YouTube found A/B results not sensitive to the algorithm. See note 24.

nodes.label: Other candidate sources
nodes.summary: Popular, trending, followed or related items blended with the embedding candidates. The YouTube paper says the design enables blending other sources; the specific sources here are our examples.

nodes.label: Ranking model
nodes.summary: Deep network scoring each impression of a few hundred candidates with hundreds of features, trained for expected watch time per impression rather than clicks.

nodes.label: Re-ranking and policy
nodes.summary: Removes ineligible or seen items, enforces diversity, adds exploration and business rules. Industry practice.

nodes.label: Feature store
nodes.summary: Online features such as recent watches, searches and impressions, defined once for training and serving to avoid skew. Serving up-to-the-second impression history is an engineering challenge in itself.

nodes.label: Item corpus and embeddings
nodes.summary: Video catalogue with embeddings used by the nearest-neighbour index; new items must enter quickly because users prefer fresh content.

nodes.label: Event log (Kafka)
nodes.summary: One Kafka queue for user actions and another for features, so a streaming job can join them.

nodes.label: Online joiner (Flink)
nodes.summary: Joins features with labels from user actions into training examples, using a unique key per request and an on-disk store for late actions; applies negative sampling with log-odds correction at serving.

nodes.label: Training (batch and online)
nodes.summary: Batch training over history, then online training on real-time examples; the training parameter servers are snapshotted daily.

nodes.label: Serving parameters
nodes.summary: Parameters the serving path uses. Changed sparse embeddings are synchronised from training at about a minute-level interval; dense parameters about daily.

nodes.label: Alternative: decide by live A/B test
nodes.summary: The YouTube paper uses offline metrics to iterate but relies on live A/B experiments for the final decision, because live results are not always correlated with offline ones.

steps.caption: The user opens the home page; the API receives user and context.
The user model builds a user embedding from history and context.
The embedding is the query for the nearest-neighbour index.
The index returns the closest videos from millions.
Hundreds of candidates go to the ranking model.
The ranker fetches many features for the user and each video.
The scored list goes to re-ranking, which applies filters and diversity.
The final list returns to the API.
The user sees dozens of videos.

flows.name: Learning from what the user does

steps.caption: Impressions and actions are logged.
The joiner pairs each action with the features shown at the time.
Training examples reach online training.
Changed sparse parameters are pushed to serving at about a minute-level interval.
The ranker uses the updated parameters on the next requests.

flows.name: An action arrives days after the impression (failure mode)

steps.caption: The impression's features were logged when it was shown.
Days later the action arrives; the in-memory cache has dropped the features, so the joiner looks in the on-disk store to pair them.
Examples keep arriving at online training.
The failed server is restored from the daily snapshot, losing up to a day of updates, which Monolith found tolerable for quality.
The API cannot get embedding candidates.
It falls back to other candidate sources such as popular items so the page is not empty (our design reasoning).
